meta.game: Pokemon Red and Blue (English, Game Boy, Gen I; not Yellow)
meta.idConventions: Species and move ids are lowercase alphanumeric Showdown ids (mrmime, farfetchd, nidoranf, nidoranm, doubleedge, softboiled). Location keys are PokeAPI location slugs from /region/kanto.
meta.stageSemantics: earliestStage = the first stage at which the thing can actually be reached, given the gym order used here (Brock, Misty, Surge, Erika, Koga, Sabrina, Blaine, Giovanni), badge requirements for field HMs, and key items picked up as soon as they're reachable. typicalStage = when a standard walkthrough gets there. They differ because Red/Blue is quite open after Cut: with the Cascade Badge you can reach Celadon, the Rocket Hideout, the Pokemon Tower, Fuchsia and the Safari Zone before beating Lt. Surge. For a 'what do I have right now' slider, typicalStage is usually the more intuitive filter.
meta.primaryTruthSource: pret/pokered disassembly (github.com/pret/pokered), cross-checked against Bulbapedia wikitext (via the MediaWiki API) and PokeAPI.

stages.label: Start: Pallet Town & Route 1
stages.summary: Choose a starter in Oak's Lab, fight the rival once, walk Route 1 to Viridian and pick up Oak's Parcel. Route 1 and Route 22 grass can be walked, but you can't buy Poke Balls until the parcel is delivered.
stages.notes: The Viridian City old man blocks the road north until Oak's Parcel is delivered.

stages.label: Pre-Brock: Viridian Forest & Pewter
stages.summary: Pokedex received and Poke Balls on sale in Viridian. Route 2 (west side), Viridian Forest, Pewter City, optional rival battle on Route 22. Ends by beating Brock (Boulder Badge).
stages.notes: A boy in Pewter blocks the east exit to Route 3 until Brock is beaten.

stages.label: Pre-Misty: Mt. Moon & Cerulean
stages.summary: Route 3, Mt. Moon (fossil choice), Route 4, Cerulean City (rival), Nugget Bridge (Routes 24/25) and Bill's S.S. Ticket. Ends by beating Misty (Cascade Badge).
stages.notes: The Boulder Badge enables Flash, but HM05 is behind a Cut tree on Route 2, so Flash can't be used yet. After meeting Bill you can already walk south to Route 5 / Vermilion through the burglarized house, so the next stage's areas are technically reachable here (see earliestStage vs typicalStage).

stages.label: Pre-Surge: Vermilion & S.S. Anne
stages.summary: Routes 5/6 and the Underground Path, Vermilion City (Old Rod, Bike Voucher), S.S. Anne (rival, HM01 Cut), Route 11 and Diglett's Cave, Route 2 east side (HM05 Flash for 10 owned), Pewter Museum Old Amber (needs Cut). Ends by beating Lt. Surge (Thunder Badge).
stages.notes: Cut becomes usable here: HM01 from the S.S. Anne captain plus the Cascade Badge. Surge's Gym is behind a Cut tree. With Cut you could already travel Route 9 to Rock Tunnel, Lavender and Celadon and beyond, so strict earliestStage values put many mid-game areas here.

stages.label: Pre-Erika: Rock Tunnel, Lavender & Celadon
stages.summary: Route 9, Rock Tunnel, Route 10, Lavender Town, Routes 8/7, Celadon City (Eevee, Game Corner prizes, Dept. Store TMs, rooftop drinks). Ends by beating Erika (Rainbow Badge).
stages.notes: The Thunder Badge enables Fly; HM02 Fly is in the Route 16 house (reached with Cut from Celadon). A drink from the Celadon rooftop vending machines gets you past the Saffron gate guards.

stages.label: Pre-Koga: Rocket Hideout, Pokemon Tower & Fuchsia
stages.summary: Rocket Hideout (Giovanni #1, Silph Scope), Pokemon Tower (rival, Mr. Fuji, Poke Flute), wake a Snorlax (Route 12 or 16), Routes 12-18 / Cycling Road, Fuchsia City (Good Rod), Safari Zone (HM03 Surf, Gold Teeth for HM04 Strength), Super Rod on Route 12. Ends by beating Koga (Soul Badge).
stages.notes: The Rainbow Badge enables Strength. HM03 Surf is found here but can't be used on the field until the Soul Badge. Gym order is flexible from here on: Bulbapedia's walkthrough does Saffron/Sabrina before Fuchsia/Koga; this file uses Erika -> Koga -> Sabrina -> Blaine -> Giovanni.

stages.label: Pre-Sabrina: Saffron & Silph Co.
stages.summary: Surf is usable. Saffron City: Fighting Dojo (Hitmonlee or Hitmonchan), Silph Co. (rival, Lapras, Giovanni #2, Master Ball). Ends by beating Sabrina (Marsh Badge).
stages.notes: Surf opens the Power Plant, Seafoam Islands, Routes 19-21 and Cinnabar, so Blaine can come before Sabrina. Saffron can be entered as early as pre-erika with a drink, and Silph Co. once Mr. Fuji is rescued.

stages.label: Pre-Blaine: Seafoam & Cinnabar
stages.summary: Routes 19/20 by sea, Seafoam Islands (Articuno), Cinnabar Island (Pokemon Lab fossil revival and trades, Pokemon Mansion and the Secret Key), Route 21. Ends by beating Blaine (Volcano Badge).
stages.notes: The Soul Badge must come before the Volcano Badge because Cinnabar can only be reached by Surf.

stages.label: Pre-Giovanni: Viridian Gym
stages.summary: Viridian Gym opens after 7 badges. The Power Plant (Zapdos) is usually cleaned up here. Ends by beating Giovanni (Earth Badge).
stages.notes: The Power Plant has been reachable since Surf (pre-sabrina).

stages.label: Elite Four: Route 22/23, Victory Road & Indigo Plateau
stages.summary: Rival on Route 22, Route 23 badge gates, Victory Road (Moltres; Strength puzzles), then Lorelei, Bruno, Agatha, Lance and the Champion.
stages.notes: Route 23 checks each badge in order; Surf and Strength are needed to reach Indigo Plateau.

stages.label: Post-game: Cerulean Cave
stages.summary: After you become Champion, the guard leaves Cerulean Cave (entered by Surf). Mewtwo is at the bottom.
stages.notes: Anything missable, like the second fossil or the other Fighting Dojo Pokemon, is gone for good.

pallet-town.name: Pallet Town
pallet-town.notes: Fishing only, from the shore south of town (the start of Route 21). No surf table.

viridian-city.name: Viridian City
viridian-city.notes: Fishing only, in the city pond.

pewter-city.name: Pewter City
pewter-city.notes: No wild Pokemon. Brock's Gym; the Pewter Museum back room (needs Cut) gives the Old Amber.

cerulean-city.name: Cerulean City
cerulean-city.notes: Fishing only (the Super Rod also works in the Cerulean Gym pool). Also has the Jynx trade and the TM28 Dig Rocket.

vermilion-city.name: Vermilion City
vermilion-city.notes: Fishing only, in the harbor and at the S.S. Anne dock. Vermilion is technically reachable pre-Misty (via Route 5 after meeting Bill), but the usual route arrives after the Cascade Badge.

celadon-city.name: Celadon City
celadon-city.notes: Fishing only, in the city pond. Eevee gift, Game Corner prize Pokemon and TMs, Dept. Store TMs, Rocket Hideout.

fuchsia-city.name: Fuchsia City
fuchsia-city.notes: Fishing only. Getting to Fuchsia takes the Poke Flute (Snorlax on Route 12 or 16), or the Bicycle via Cycling Road, which also needs the Route 16 Snorlax woken.

cinnabar-island.name: Cinnabar Island
cinnabar-island.notes: Fishing only. The Pokemon Lab revives fossils and hosts 3 trades. Reached by Surf (Route 20 or 21), which needs the Soul Badge.

saffron-city.name: Saffron City
saffron-city.notes: No wild Pokemon. Fighting Dojo (Hitmonlee/Hitmonchan) and Silph Co. (Lapras). The gate guards let you in after you hand over a drink from the Celadon rooftop. The Rocket at Silph Co.'s door leaves once Mr. Fuji is rescued.

kanto-route-1.name: Route 1
kanto-route-1.notes: Pidgey and Rattata. Catching needs Poke Balls, which go on sale after Oak's Parcel is delivered.

kanto-route-22.name: Route 22
kanto-route-22.notes: West of Viridian. Grass is reachable from the start (Poke Balls come after the parcel). Water is fishable.

kanto-route-2.name: Route 2
kanto-route-2.notes: One grass table covers the whole route. The east side (Mr. Mime trade house, HM05 Flash gate) needs Cut or Diglett's Cave.

viridian-forest.name: Viridian Forest
viridian-forest.notes: Bug Pokemon, plus Pikachu at a low rate.

kanto-route-3.name: Route 3
kanto-route-3.notes: Needs the Boulder Badge, because the Pewter boy blocks the exit until Brock is beaten.

mt-moon.name: Mt. Moon
mt-moon.notes: 1F, B1F and B2F. Clefairy are rare. Choose the Dome or Helix Fossil at B2F. The Magikarp salesman is in the Pokemon Center outside (Route 4).

kanto-route-4.name: Route 4
kanto-route-4.notes: Grass east of Mt. Moon. The pond near Cerulean has a Super Rod table too (not in PokeAPI).

kanto-route-24.name: Route 24 (Nugget Bridge)
kanto-route-24.notes: Nugget Bridge north of Cerulean. Red/Blue grass tables differ.

kanto-route-25.name: Route 25
kanto-route-25.notes: Leads to Bill's Sea Cottage (S.S. Ticket).

kanto-route-5.name: Route 5
kanto-route-5.notes: South of Cerulean. Reachable pre-Misty through the burglarized house after meeting Bill, or with Cut. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-underground-path.name: Underground Path (Routes 5-6)
kanto-underground-path.notes: No wild Pokemon. The Nidoran trade is in the Route 5 entrance building.

kanto-route-6.name: Route 6
kanto-route-6.notes: North of Vermilion. Red/Blue tables differ.

ss-anne.name: S.S. Anne
ss-anne.notes: No wild Pokemon. Rival battle, HM01 Cut from the captain, TM08 and TM44. The ship leaves for good once you have Cut.

kanto-route-11.name: Route 11
kanto-route-11.notes: East of Vermilion. The Nidorina trade is in the gate. Snorlax at the east end blocks Route 12. Red/Blue tables differ.

digletts-cave.name: Diglett's Cave
digletts-cave.notes: Links Route 11 (near Vermilion) to Route 2's east side. Diglett and Dugtrio only.

kanto-route-9.name: Route 9
kanto-route-9.notes: A Cut tree east of Cerulean blocks the way. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-10.name: Route 10
kanto-route-10.notes: Around Rock Tunnel. You need Surf to reach the Power Plant from here.

rock-tunnel.name: Rock Tunnel
rock-tunnel.notes: Dark without Flash (Flash is optional). PokeAPI areas rock-tunnel-b1f/b2f match pokered's 1F/B1F.

lavender-town.name: Lavender Town
lavender-town.notes: No wild Pokemon. Mr. Fuji's house (Poke Flute after the Tower).

kanto-route-8.name: Route 8
kanto-route-8.notes: West of Lavender, linked to Route 7 by the Underground Path. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-7.name: Route 7
kanto-route-7.notes: East of Celadon. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-12.name: Route 12
kanto-route-12.notes: The only grass patch is south of the Snorlax, down a Cut path. The Silence Bridge piers north of the Snorlax can be fished as soon as you reach Lavender. Snorlax (Lv30) is here. The Super Rod house is south of the Snorlax, and the Lavender gate 2F gives TM39 Swift. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-13.name: Route 13
kanto-route-13.notes: Reached past a Snorlax (Route 12) or from Fuchsia. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-15.name: Route 15
kanto-route-15.notes: West of Fuchsia. TM20 Rage needs Cut. Red/Blue tables differ.

kanto-route-16.name: Route 16
kanto-route-16.notes: The grass is in the north half, past a Cut tree just west of Celadon, so the Snorlax isn't needed for it. The Fly house is there too. Snorlax (Lv30) blocks the main road to Cycling Road.

kanto-route-17.name: Route 17 (Cycling Road)
kanto-route-17.notes: Needs the Bicycle and the Route 16 Snorlax woken. Fishing works here in Gen I, but Surf is not allowed.

kanto-route-18.name: Route 18
kanto-route-18.notes: The grass is on the Fuchsia side, so no bike is needed; the gate westward toward Cycling Road requires the Bicycle. The Lickitung trade is in the gate 2F.

kanto-safari-zone.name: Safari Zone
kanto-safari-zone.notes: Fuchsia. ¥500 entry for 30 Safari Balls and 500 steps. Four areas: middle, east, north, west. The Super Rod can hook Dratini here. HM03 Surf (Secret House) and the Gold Teeth (for HM04 Strength) are inside.

pokemon-tower.name: Pokemon Tower
pokemon-tower.notes: Wild Pokemon live on 3F-7F. Unidentified 'GHOST's can't be caught, so the Silph Scope from the Rocket Hideout is required. The rival battle on 2F doesn't need the Scope.

kanto-power-plant.name: Power Plant
kanto-power-plant.notes: Surf from Route 10. Zapdos (Lv50), plus 6 Voltorb (Lv40) and 2 Electrode (Lv43) disguised as items. Electabuzz is wild in Red only. Optional; Bulbapedia's walkthrough visits it just before the Viridian Gym.

kanto-sea-route-19.name: Route 19 (Sea Route)
kanto-sea-route-19.notes: South of Fuchsia. The beach at the north end can be fished without Surf. The surf table is Tentacool only.

kanto-sea-route-20.name: Route 20 (Sea Route)
kanto-sea-route-20.notes: Between Route 19 and Cinnabar. Seafoam Islands sit in the middle. The surf table is Tentacool only.

seafoam-islands.name: Seafoam Islands
seafoam-islands.notes: Needs Surf. Strength (push boulders to calm the currents) is needed to reach the fishable water on B3F/B4F and Articuno (Lv50, B4F). In caves the land table also applies while surfing.

pokemon-mansion.name: Pokemon Mansion
pokemon-mansion.notes: Cinnabar. Holds the Secret Key for Cinnabar Gym, plus TM14 and TM22 on B1F. Red/Blue tables differ (Growlithe in Red, Vulpix in Blue; Magmar only in Blue).

kanto-sea-route-21.name: Route 21 (Sea Route)
kanto-sea-route-21.notes: South of Pallet by Surf. It has a grass patch on land plus a surf table.

kanto-route-23.name: Route 23
kanto-route-23.notes: Badge checkpoints in badge order. The water is past the 4th (Rainbow) checkpoint, and the grass is past the 6th (Marsh) checkpoint and needs Surf. Most players first come here heading to Victory Road.

kanto-victory-road-2.name: Victory Road
kanto-victory-road-2.notes: PokeAPI slug kanto-victory-road-2 is the Gen I-III Kanto Victory Road; kanto-victory-road-1 is the Gen II/IV one. Needs all 8 badges (Route 23 gate) and Strength. Moltres (Lv50) is on 2F.

indigo-plateau.name: Indigo Plateau
indigo-plateau.notes: No wild Pokemon. The Elite Four and the Champion.

cerulean-cave.name: Cerulean Cave
cerulean-cave.notes: Opens after you become Champion. Entered by Surf from Cerulean. Mewtwo (Lv70) is on B1F. Super Rod table: Slowbro, Seaking, Kingler, Seadra (Lv23).

Give nidorino, get nidorina nicknamed TERRY. It arrives at the same level as the Pokemon you trade away. Traded Pokemon gain boosted EXP but disobey above your badge obedience cap. Same trade in English Red and Blue.

It comes from the Super Rod at Celadon City or Route 10 (Lv23), or from evolving a rod-caught Poliwag at Lv25, so the stages reflect when you can get a Poliwhirl.

versionExclusives.notes: Species obtainable, by catching or evolving, in only one version. Scyther and Pinsir are also Game Corner prizes, but only in the version that already has them in the Safari Zone. Game Corner prices and levels for Abra, Clefairy, Dratini and Porygon differ by version; Red sells Nidorina and Blue sells Nidorino, but both are wild in both versions. Electabuzz is wild in the Power Plant in Red only; Magmar is wild in the Pokemon Mansion in Blue only.

unobtainable.notes: Only from official distribution events (or glitches). It can't be obtained in normal Red/Blue play.

unobtainableNotes: Every other species is obtainable across both versions together. Without trading, each version is missing its counterpart's exclusives plus the trade evolutions (Alakazam, Machamp, Golem, Gengar). NPC-trade-only species (Mr. Mime, Farfetch'd, Jynx, Lickitung) are available in both versions from in-game trades. Missing in Red alone (no trading): sandshrew, sandslash, vulpix, ninetales, meowth, persian, alakazam, machamp, bellsprout, weepinbell, victreebel, golem, gengar, magmar, pinsir, mew. Missing in Blue alone: ekans, arbok, oddish, gloom, vileplume, mankey, primeape, growlithe, arcanine, alakazam, machamp, golem, gengar, scyther, electabuzz, mew.

trainers.name: Brock
trainers.notes: Onix's Bide is its gym-leader signature move.

trainers.name: Misty
trainers.notes: Starmie's BubbleBeam is its signature move (it replaces Harden).

trainers.name: Lt. Surge
trainers.notes: Raichu's Thunderbolt replaces Thunder Wave.

trainers.name: Erika
trainers.notes: Vileplume's Mega Drain is its signature move.

trainers.name: Koga
trainers.notes: Weezing's Toxic is its signature move.

trainers.name: Sabrina
trainers.notes: Alakazam's Psywave is its signature move (it replaces Psychic). You can fight Sabrina before Koga; Bulbapedia's walkthrough does.

trainers.name: Blaine
trainers.notes: Arcanine's Fire Blast is its signature move. The Gym needs the Secret Key from the Pokemon Mansion.

trainers.name: Giovanni
trainers.notes: Rhydon's Fissure is its signature move (slot 3). The Gym is locked until you have the other 7 badges.

trainers.name: Lorelei
trainers.notes: Lapras has Blizzard (Elite Four signature move in slot 3). All four must be beaten in a row.

trainers.name: Bruno
trainers.notes: Machamp has Fissure (slot 3). Both Onix are Rock/Ground, not Fighting. All four must be beaten in a row.

trainers.name: Agatha
trainers.notes: The Lv60 Gengar has Toxic (slot 3). In Gen I her Ghost moves can't touch Psychic types and Night Shade does fixed damage equal to the user's level. All four must be beaten in a row.

trainers.name: Lance
trainers.notes: Dragonite has Barrier (slot 3). Only Dragonite and the Dragonairs are Dragon type; Dragon Rage always does 40 HP. All four must be beaten in a row.

trainers.name: Rival (1) - Oak's Lab
trainers.notes: Unavoidable first battle. You can lose it without penalty. Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (2) - Route 22
trainers.notes: Optional. Only appears after delivering Oak's Parcel and before beating Brock. Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (3) - Cerulean City
trainers.locationDetail: North Cerulean, south end of Nugget Bridge
trainers.notes: Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (4) - S.S. Anne
trainers.notes: Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (5) - Pokemon Tower
trainers.notes: Doesn't need the Silph Scope, so it can be fought on your first visit to Lavender (pre-erika). Bulbapedia's walkthrough has it after Celadon. Bulbapedia lists the player-Charmander Growlithe (Lv23) as Bite/Roar/Ember, but Growlithe learns Leer at Lv23 (pokered), so the computed set includes Leer. Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (6) - Silph Co.
trainers.notes: Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Rival (7) - Route 22
trainers.notes: Appears after the Earth Badge. Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. The rival's team varies with it.

trainers.name: Champion (Rival)
trainers.notes: Keyed by the starter the PLAYER picked. Custom moves: Pidgeot Sky Attack, plus the starter gets Mega Drain (Venusaur), Fire Blast (Charizard) or Blizzard (Blastoise), all in slot 3.

trainers.name: Giovanni (Rocket Hideout)
trainers.locationDetail: Rocket Hideout B4F (under the Game Corner)
trainers.notes: Drops the Silph Scope. Possible as early as pre-erika (strict: pre-surge). Bulbapedia's walkthrough clears the Hideout after Erika.

trainers.name: Giovanni (Silph Co.)

mechanicsNotes: Gen I has a single Special stat that powers special attacks and defends against them.

Physical or special depends on the move's type: Normal, Fighting, Flying, Poison, Ground, Rock, Bug and Ghost moves are physical; Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Ice, Psychic and Dragon moves are special.
Critical-hit chance is based on base Speed (about base Speed / 512), times 8 for Slash, Razor Leaf, Crabhammer and Karate Chop, so fast Pokemon crit far more often.
Critical hits double the attacker's level in the damage formula and ignore all stat stages, both good and bad.
Focus Energy and Dire Hit are bugged: they divide your critical-hit chance by 4 instead of raising it.
Ghost moves have no effect on Psychic types (the official chart said 2x). The only damaging Ghost moves are Lick and Night Shade (fixed damage), so Ghost gives no real answer to Psychic.
Psychic types dominate Gen I: Bug moves are weak (Pin Missile, Twineedle, Leech Life), Ghost is useless against them, and Dark and Steel don't exist yet.
Other Gen I type-chart differences: Bug is super effective against Poison, Poison is super effective against Bug, and Ice is neutral against Fire.
Badge boosts multiply a stat by 1.125 in battle: Boulder = Attack, Thunder = Defense, Soul = Speed, Volcano = Special. A glitch reapplies them whenever any stat stage changes.
Obedience for traded Pokemon: up to Lv10 with no badges, 30 with Cascade, 50 with Rainbow, 70 with Marsh, and all levels with Earth.
Field HMs need badges: Flash = Boulder, Cut = Cascade, Fly = Thunder, Strength = Rainbow, Surf = Soul.
Hyper Beam skips its recharge turn if it knocks the target out, breaks a Substitute, or misses.
Wrap, Bind, Fire Spin and Clamp stop the target from acting for 2-5 turns, which makes fast users very strong.
Every move has an extra 1/256 chance to miss (a 100%-accuracy move hits 255/256 of the time); in English R/B, Swift and Bide skip the accuracy check.
Freeze never thaws on its own; only a Fire move that can burn, Haze, or an Ice Heal / Full Heal cures it, so Blizzard (90% accuracy, 10% freeze in English R/B) is very strong.
Sleep lasts 1-7 turns, and the Pokemon can't act on the turn it wakes up.
Paralysis quarters Speed and gives about a 25% chance each turn of being fully paralyzed.
Explosion (170 power) and Self-Destruct (130) halve the target's Defense, and in Gen I the user doesn't faint if the move breaks a Substitute.
Substitute costs 25% of max HP. Using it at exactly 25% HP makes the user faint.
Toxic's counter also ramps up Leech Seed damage, and in Gen I Toxic reverts to regular poison when the Pokemon switches out.
Counter only reflects Normal- and Fighting-type damage.
Night Shade and Seismic Toss deal damage equal to the user's level; Dragon Rage always deals 40 and Sonic Boom always deals 20.
Reflect and Light Screen double the user's Defense or Special against incoming damage; the effect belongs to that Pokemon (lost on switching or Haze), and critical hits ignore it.
Gym leaders and the Elite Four use level-up movesets (the last 4 moves learned by their level) plus one signature move written to slot 3 of one Pokemon.
Traded Pokemon gain 1.5x EXP. The trade evolutions Alakazam, Machamp, Golem and Gengar need a real trade.
Only one Eevee, one Lapras, one Hitmon, one Mt. Moon fossil and one Old Amber per game; most other statics are one-shot, so a knockout loses them.
